The company claims its model is built from scratch to predict human behavior. Mirror Particle argues that large‑language‑model role‑play falls short for market research and brand strategy. The launch will take place at the TechCrunch Disrupt event.
summary: Mirror Particle will launch a world model built from scratch to predict human behavior at TechCrunch Disrupt's Startup Battlefield 200. Mirror Particle argues that LLM role-play falls short for market research and brand strategy.
author: TechCrunch

title: JioHotstar to be offered inside Starzplay, not as stand‑alone service
content: India’s JioHotstar is expanding into the Middle East by partnering with Starzplay. The Indian streaming service will be offered inside Starzplay rather than through a stand‑alone service. This arrangement allows JioHotstar to reach Middle Eastern viewers directly within the Starzplay platform.
summary: JioHotstar will be available within the Starzplay platform. It will not launch as a separate, stand‑alone service.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI agents face website blocks and anti-bot defenses, new standard proposed
content:
Personal AI agents promise to shop, book flights, and make reservations for users.  

However, deliberate blocks and anti‑bot defenses are increasingly preventing these agents from accessing websites, leaving consumers caught in the middle.  

A new standard is being developed to address these obstacles.
summary: Personal AI agents can shop, book flights, and make reservations, but website blocks and anti-bot defenses hinder them. A new standard is being developed to address these barriers.
author: TechCrunch

title: Lambda to raise $4B ahead of 2027 IPO, led by Coatue and Blackstone
content: AI computing startup Lambda has announced it will raise up to $4 billion in a funding round that values the company at $14.5 billion pre‑money. The round is led by investment firms Coatue and Blackstone. Lambda, which is backed by Nvidia, plans to use the capital to prepare for an initial public offering scheduled for 2027.
summary: Nvidia-backed Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre‑money valuation. The funding round is led by Coatue and Blackstone and precedes the company’s planned 2027 IPO.
author: TechCrunch

title: Musubi Unveils PolicyLM-1.7B, Lightweight Real-Time Moderation Model with Open Weights
content:
Musubi announced on Tuesday the release of a new lightweight decision model designed for real‑time content moderation. The model, named PolicyLM‑1.7B, is intended to provide rapid moderation decisions in live environments.  

PolicyLM‑1.7B was released with open weights, allowing developers to access and integrate the model into their moderation workflows.
summary: Musubi announced the lightweight decision model PolicyLM-1.7B on Tuesday. The model is designed for real-time moderation and was released with open weights.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI wunderkind Sigil Wen launches Underdog, the most private Instinct/Muse rival
content:
Sigil Wen, an AI wunderkind, has launched Underdog, an on‑device assistant that competes with Instinct and Muse.  

Underdog is described as free, fully private, and capable of handling everyday tasks. The project is backed by a Silicon Valley's who‑who.  

Underdog positions itself as the most private competitor in the Instinct/Muse market.
summary: Sigil Wen, backed by a Silicon Valley's who-who, has launched Underdog, an on-device AI assistant. Underdog promises to be free, fully private and capable for everyday tasks.
author: TechCrunch

title: Three Iranians on trial in London for alleged plot against UK-based Iran dissident journalists
content:
Three Iranian nationals are on trial in London over an alleged plot to target journalists who oppose the regime in Tehran. The defendants face accusations of planning attacks against UK‑based journalists identified as dissidents.

The case is being heard in a London court, where prosecutors say the three men intended to target the journalists because of their opposition to the Iranian government.
summary: Three Iranians are on trial in London. They are accused of targeting UK-based journalists opposed to the regime in Tehran.
author: Euronews

title: Expert says Brazil has shifted rightward; Flavio Bolsonaro gets right-wing endorsements
content:
Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has secured endorsements from right‑wing politicians Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, both of whom opposed him in Sunday’s first‑round vote, as he prepares for a runoff against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva later this month.  

Anthony Pereira, executive director of the Stone Center for Latin American Studies at Tulane University, told France 24’s Sharon Gaffney that Brazil “has moved to the right progressively over the last two decades.” He added that Lula’s path to victory depends on mobilising voters who did not participate in the first round, while Bolsonaro is likely to benefit from voters who supported other right‑wing candidates and may shift to him, making his prospects in the second round appear stronger.  

The runoff election is set for later this month.
summary: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro received endorsements from Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema for the runoff against President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Anthony Pereira, Executive Director of the Stone Center for Latin American Studies at Tulane University, said Lula must mobilize non‑voters from the first round while Bolsonaro is likely to pick up voters from other right‑wing candidates, making his path to victory easier.
author: France 24

title: Reed Brody says Christa Pike's botched execution shows systemic US death penalty flaws
content:
Jean‑Emile Jammine welcomed Reed Brody, an international human‑rights lawyer and former New York assistant attorney general, to discuss the botched execution of Christa Pike. Brody said the failed lethal injection illustrates a broader problem linking capital punishment, institutional failure, due‑process concerns and human dignity.

He noted that the technical malfunction exposes weaknesses throughout the legal architecture of the death penalty, including the quality and adequacy of defense representation, stark disparities between jurisdictions and the difficulties states encounter in carrying out executions.
summary: Jean-Emile Jammine welcomed Reed Brody, an international human rights lawyer and former New York assistant attorney general. Brody said the botched lethal‑injection execution of Christa Pike reveals broader problems in the U.S. death‑penalty system, including defense quality, jurisdictional disparities and state execution challenges.
author: France 24

title: France sees civil servants join high school protests over classroom conditions
content:
A protest movement erupted in France as civil servants joined high‑school students who entered their third week of picketing over long‑deteriorating classroom conditions. The demonstration caught a broke, lame‑duck French government off guard, according to the report.

The unrest has been described as “surprise” and has already seen violence, prompting concerns that authorities may respond with a heavy hand. French officials have historically matched protest‑related violence with strong police action, a strategy that has previously turned the silent majority against demonstrators, as observed during the pre‑Covid Yellow Vests movement.

The escalation of the current protests risks a similar shift in public sentiment, potentially isolating the demonstrators from broader support.
summary: Civil servants joined high schoolers on Tuesday in the third week of picketing over long‑deteriorating classroom conditions. The surprise protest has faced a heavy‑handed response that, in past movements such as the pre‑Covid Yellow Vests, turned the silent majority against the protesters.
author: France 24

title: France sees 250,000 students, unions, teachers protest for better learning conditions
content:
A quarter of a million demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday as unions and teachers joined high‑school students demanding better learning conditions. The mass movement, reported by FRANCE 24 from central Paris, later saw sporadic clashes with security forces.

A French policeman was charged with violence after prosecutors said he fired a tear‑gas grenade at close range at a 14‑year‑old student during the protests. The incident occurred amid the broader demonstrations that have shaken the country.

FRANCE 24’s Claire Paccalin quoted protesters saying, “this is not it, this movement will continue, we want concrete actions from the government.”
summary: A quarter of a million demonstrators, including high‑school students, unions and teachers, marched across France demanding better learning conditions, and the protests later saw sporadic clashes with security forces. A French policeman was charged with violence for firing a tear‑gas grenade at close range at a 14‑year‑old student during the demonstrations.
author: France 24

title: Hundreds of thousands of French students protest school conditions nationwide
content:
Hundreds of thousands of students and their supporters took part in nationwide protests across France on Tuesday, following weeks of student‑built barricades that targeted school conditions. The demonstrations, which began in Paris, quickly spread to other regions, reflecting a broad wave of discontent among pupils.

Organizers and participants described the action as a rising movement that shows no sign of slowing, underscoring the scale of frustration with the state of French schools. The coordinated protests marked another major episode in the ongoing campaign by students to demand improvements to their educational environment.
summary: Hundreds of thousands of students and their supporters took part in nationwide protests across France on Tuesday. The protests came after weeks of student barricades protesting school conditions.
author: France 24

title: Former BND chief August Hanning arrested on espionage and treason charges
content: German former spy chief August Hanning was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of espionage and treason. Hanning, who headed Germany’s BND foreign‑intelligence agency from 1998 to 2005, is accused of working for foreign intelligence services and of espionage and treason, prosecutors said. The arrest comes at a time when Germany is seeking to broaden the powers of its intelligence agencies. The case was reported by Nick Holdsworth of France 24 from Berlin.
summary: A former German spy chief was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of espionage and treason. Prosecutors said August Hanning, who led the BND from 1998 to 2005, is accused of espionage, treason and working for foreign intelligence services.
author: France 24

title: French mayors urge temporary block of social media for minors amid student protests
content:
Student protests in France are being amplified by social media, with artificial intelligence further boosting the reach of demonstrators, according to reports.  

Some French mayors have responded by calling for social media platforms to be temporarily blocked for minors, citing the role of these services in accelerating the protests.  

France 2 has examined the impact of these developments on the movement.
summary: Some French mayors have called for social media platforms to be temporarily blocked for minors. The calls come as student protests are being accelerated by social media, which is further boosted by artificial intelligence.
author: France 24

title: Seventh arrest made over UK airbase incident linked to US strikes
content:
A seventh man was arrested on Tuesday over a major incident last month at RAF Fairford, a British military airbase used by the United States to launch strikes on Iran, police said.

The arrest came a day after President Donald Trump announced that the United States had withdrawn all B‑1 bombers from RAF Fairford because of "threats" he believed were linked to Tehran. The 22‑year‑old British male was arrested in London "on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts," Britain's Counter‑Terrorism Policing network said in a statement. Six men in their 20s had already been arrested and released on bail after three suspicious vans were stopped near the base in southwest England on September 27.

Bénédicte Paviot reports from London.
summary: Police arrested a seventh man on Tuesday over a major incident at RAF Fairford, a British airbase used by the United States to launch strikes on Iran. The arrest follows six earlier arrests of men in their 20s who were released on bail after three suspicious vans were stopped near the base in southwest England on September 27.
author: France 24

title: European Commission proposes ideas to ease EU expansion and address member concerns
content:
The European Commission has presented ideas intended to make the European Union’s expansion process more acceptable to current members. The proposals aim to simplify accession procedures and address concerns raised by existing states.

Among the countries seeking membership are several candidates, including war‑torn Ukraine. The Commission’s initiative seeks to balance the Union’s enlargement ambitions with the sensitivities of its present members.
summary: The European Commission has put forward ideas to ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, including war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.
author: DW World

title: WHO monitors possible plague case after lab worker dies in Siberia, Russia
content:
The death of a lab worker in Russia’s Siberia region has raised concerns about a possible plague case, the United Nations World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.  

WHO added that it was following the situation closely and that testing and monitoring are underway.
summary: The death of a lab worker in Russia’s Siberia region has raised concerns about a possible plague case. The UN World Health Organization said it is closely following the situation.
author: UN News

title: Djibouti faces overlapping emergencies as Yemen refugees arrive, migrants depart, IOM warns
content:
Djibouti is confronting “overlapping emergencies,” according to a warning issued by the UN migration agency (IOM) on Tuesday.

The country is receiving refugees fleeing the conflict in Yemen, who are arriving on its shores. At the same time, migrants continue to travel in the opposite direction, adding to the strain on Djibouti’s resources.
summary: Djibouti is facing overlapping emergencies as refugees fleeing the conflict in Yemen arrive on its shores. The UN migration agency (IOM) warned on Tuesday that migrants continue traveling in the opposite direction.
author: UN News

title: Super El Niño Drives Drought in Papua New Guinea
content:
Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing, and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected.  

The warning signs are linked to an El Niño event whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the levels recorded during the historic 1997 and 2015 events.  The pattern is being described by some climate watchers as a “Super El Niño.”  

The expanding reach of this El Niño is already affecting water availability, crop yields, and food costs in the region.
summary: Water sources are drying up, crops are failing, and food prices are rising in Papua New Guinea. The Pacific Ocean temperatures of this El Niño have already surpassed those of the historic 1997 and 2015 events, and it is being dubbed a “Super El Niño” by some climate watchers.
author: UN News

title: Trinidad and Tobago journalists demand amendment to 2026 special operations bill
content:
Journalists in Trinidad and Tobago have demanded an urgent amendment to the Special Operations Bill 2026, arguing that the legislation’s expanded police search and seizure powers threaten the nation’s long‑standing press freedom.

The bill, which was passed on 24 September, grants law‑enforcement agencies broader authority to conduct searches and seize property, prompting media representatives to call for changes to protect journalistic activity. 

The government defended the legislation, stating it is intended to address the country’s alarmingly high crime and murder rates.
summary: Journalists in Trinidad and Tobago have called for an urgent amendment to the special operations bill 2026, which expands police search and seizure powers. The government says the bill, passed on 24 September, is intended to tackle the country’s high crime and murder rates.
author: Guardian World

title: Josh Rushing examines cracks in MAGA during Trump's second term
content:
Josh Rushing explores the fractures emerging within the MAGA movement during Donald Trump’s second term. The analysis focuses on two key areas: the Epstein files and the war on Iran.

Rushing’s examination highlights how these issues are revealing cracks in the movement’s cohesion, underscoring the challenges faced by MAGA supporters in the current political landscape.
summary: Josh Rushing examines cracks forming within MAGA during Trump's second term. He highlights issues ranging from the Epstein files to the war on Iran.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK Green Party adopts resolution calling Zionism a form of racism
content: The UK’s Green Party has adopted a new resolution that declares Zionism to be a form of racism. The resolution, which was passed by the party, states that the answer to the question “Is Zionism a form of racism?” is yes.
summary: The UK's Green Party adopted a new resolution. The resolution states that Zionism is a form of racism.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Messi super fan Yadil M Iqbal flies from Kerala to Buenos Aires for final game
content:
A Lionel Messi super fan named Yadil M Iqbal journeyed from Kerala, India, to Buenos Aires, Argentina, to attend what is being described as the star’s last game.

Iqbal’s trip took him across continents so he could watch Messi play in person at the match in Buenos Aires.
summary: Lionel Messi super fan Yadil M Iqbal traveled from Kerala, India, to Buenos Aires. He went to watch Messi play his last game.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US lawmakers urge Israel to release doctor Hussam Abu Safia
content:
US lawmakers, led by progressive members of the House of Representatives, have publicly urged Israel to release Dr. Hussam Abu Safia, a Palestinian medical worker currently imprisoned.

The representatives said their appeal is intended to draw attention to what they describe as Israeli abuse and the detention of the Palestinian doctor.
summary: Progressive US representatives have called on Israel to release doctor Hussam Abu Safia, a Palestinian medical worker who is imprisoned. They say the detention highlights Israeli abuse.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Death row inmate Christa Pike remains conscious after botched execution, lawyers say
content:
US death row inmate Christa Pike is reported to be conscious after a failed execution, her lawyers said.  

Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in a hospital, according to a statement from her lawyers on Tuesday.
summary: Christa Pike, a 50‑year‑old death row inmate, is reported to be conscious after a failed execution. Her lawyers said on Tuesday that she remains handcuffed in a hospital receiving critical medical care.
author: BBC World

title: Police use tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests spread across France
content:
Police deployed tear‑gas canisters in Paris and Marseille as school‑related demonstrations expanded across France.  

The gatherings were composed largely of teenagers who marched to demand additional resources for schools and an end to what they described as police repression.  

The use of tear gas in the two cities marked a sharp escalation as the protests continued to spread nationwide.
summary: Police deployed tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grew nationwide. The mainly teenage crowds called for more resources for schools and an end to what they called police repression.
author: BBC World

title: Axe used by Jack Nicholson in The Shining for sale as part of Stanley Kubrick auction
content:
A special‑effects axe used by Jack Nicholson in the 1980 horror film The Shining will be sold as part of Stanley Kubrick’s personal archive auction.

The axe was wielded by Nicholson’s character, Jack Torrance, when he delivered the line “Here’s Johnny!” and was used to hack a locked door protecting his wife Wendy, played by Shelley Duvall. It also served as the murder weapon in the killing of Scatman Crothers’ character, Dick Hallorann.

The item is listed for a price between £30,000 and £50,000.
summary: Exclusive: Weapon is one of hundreds of items to be sold as part of the influential late director’s personal archiveA special effects axe wielded by Jack Nicholson as he delivered his chillingly manic line “Here’s Johnny!” in the 1980 horror movie The Shining is to go on sale. Nicholson’s character, Jack Torrance, uses an axe to hack out an opening in a locked door protecting his terrified wife Wendy, played by Shelley Duvall.
author: Guardian Culture

title: George Fenton, Oscar‑nominated British composer for over 100 films, dies at 76
content:
George Fenton, the British composer who earned five Oscar nominations for scores to films such as Gandhi and Dangerous Liaisons, has died aged 76.

Fenton’s career included scores for Gandhi, Groundhog Day, and 18 Ken Loach films, as well as BBC TV news themes and Blue Planet. A statement from his family said his death was “unexpected” but did not give a cause.

The statement added that he was survived by various family members, as well as “a life of music”.
summary: George Fenton, a British composer who earned five Oscar nominations for scores to films such as Gandhi and Dangerous Liaisons, died at 76. His family said his death was unexpected and he is survived by various family members.
author: Guardian Culture

title: V/H/S/Mixtape review: Gwar hosts music‑themed horror shorts with murderous puppets
content:
The latest installment in the V/H/S horror series, V/H/S/Mixtape, features a collection of five mini-movies centered on themes of music and sound. The anthology is hosted by the metal band Gwar, whose members appear in extravagant outfits delivering Halloween-themed jokes in the interstitial segments. The shorts are connected by minimal narrative tissue, resulting in a diverse mix of content that varies significantly in both length and quality.

Among the entries is Another Cabin, a stop-motion short by Flying Lotus that depicts a young boy in a rural cabin with a mean old grannie. The plot involves a tentacled demon tearing the roof of the house in search of a snack, while the characters’ resemblance to the cast of the early 2000s series The PJs is noted. The review describes the film’s brevity as a strength despite the tonal differences.

Renee Zhan’s Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance serves as the opener, telling the story of murderous puppets taking revenge on visiting studio executives who attempt to “reimagine” ageing intellectual property. Although the segment is described as dragging on, it maintains a reasonable balance of gags and gore. The puppets, designed by Jim Henson’s Creature Shop, perform a bright major-scale title song about how all things must die, which is cited as the funniest gag in the film.
summary: Gwar hosts the V/H/S/Mixtape, a collection of music‑themed horror shorts featuring murderous puppets and stop‑motion segments. The series includes a stop‑motion piece by Flying Lotus and a puppet revenge story by Renee Zhan, with Gwar members cracking Halloween dad jokes in between.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Silver Pines review – a stylish, neo-noir detective drama
content:
Silver Pines, a neo-noir detective drama developed by Scandinavian studio Wych Elm Games and published by Team 17, is available on PC, PS5, and Switch 2. The game casts players as Red Walker, a private eye tasked with finding missing singer-songwriter Eddie Velvet in a deserted town. While the official reason for the town’s evacuation is an incoming storm, the narrative quickly reveals darker undercurrents, including the possibility that the missing musician may have committed a murder.

Set in a 2D Metroidvania-style universe, the gameplay involves exploring abandoned shops, ruined apartment buildings, and rotting sewer networks. Players solve puzzles and gather clues, such as newspaper stories and statues, to unlock new areas and advance the mystery. Progression is tied to payphones scattered throughout the town, which serve as save points but require a dollar to use.
summary: PC, PS5, Switch 2; Wych Elm Games, Team 17Abandoned shops, ruined apartment buildings and rotting sewer networks make up a dark landscape in which you play a private eye searching for a missing singer-songwriterIn a weird deserted town miles from anywhere, a troubled detective searches for a missing musician and the girl he may or may not have murdered. It could be a Silent Hill game or a lost David Lynch movie from the 1990s – in fact, it’s neither.
author: Guardian Culture

title: French filmmaker Alice Diop unveils debut installation Geste de Consolation in Paris
content:
French filmmaker Alice Diop is presenting her debut installation, Geste de Consolation, in the 60-meter-long central hall of the Palais d’Iena in Paris. The exhibition features works by various artists, writers, composers, and poets, a curation Diop describes as bringing together women who nourish her. She recently returned to France from California, where she participated in a two-week celebration of her work organized by the French department at the University of California, Berkeley.

During the Berkeley event, academics examined Diop’s documentaries Nous (We) and Vers La Tendresse (Towards Tenderness), as well as her first feature film, Saint Omer. The courtroom drama, which received the Silver Lion at Venice in 2022, was inspired by a real trial of a Senegalese woman who allowed her baby to drown. The film explores race, culture, and motherhood in contemporary France and was the first work by a black female director to be entered by France as its official entry for the 2023 Academy Awards.
summary: Alice Diop's debut installation Geste de Consolation is set in the 60‑meter central hall of Paris's Palais d’Iena, featuring works by artists, writers, composers and poets. Diop, who recently returned to France from California, previously earned a Silver Lion for her film Saint Omer and became the first black female director whose film was entered by France for the 2023 Academy Awards.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Mom Kristin Bride fights Congress for social media reform after son's suicide
content:
A new documentary follows Kristin Bride, who is advocating for social media reform in Congress following the suicide of her 16-year-old son, who was a victim of cyberbullying. The film highlights her ongoing efforts to address the impact of online harassment, encapsulated by her statement, “We’re not going to go away.”

The narrative contextualizes Bride’s fight within the broader societal reliance on smartphones, noting that devices have become essential tools for navigation, distraction, and social media engagement. The source suggests that while individuals may feel dependent on the attention economy, the industry actually relies more heavily on users than vice versa.
summary: A new documentary follows Kristin Bride as she takes on Congress after the death of her 16-year-old son who was cyberbullied. The film highlights her campaign for social media reform in response to her son's suicide.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Lena Martell, first solo Scottish female UK chart-topper, dies aged 86
content:
Lena Martell, a Glasgow-born singer and television host, has died at the age of 86. She achieved significant recognition in the music industry as a pioneering figure for Scottish artists.

Martell made history as the first solo Scottish female singer to top the UK singles chart with her hit song "One Day at a Time."
summary: Glasgow-born singer and television host Lena Martell has died at the age of 86. She was the first solo Scottish female singer to top the UK singles chart with the song One Day at a Time.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: London Broncos await Super League promotion decision after Championship Grand Final win
content:
London Broncos have dominated the second tier, winning 26 of 27 games, but promotion to Super League is not decided solely on the pitch.  

Two years ago this week the club was relegated from Super League after their ground flooded and their owner walked away following a £24 million personal investment.  The club then asked supporters to help, and fans wore last year’s away jersey emblazoned with the names of those saviours—among them the author’s own name—during the Sunday match when London thrashed Doncaster 78‑6 in the Championship Grand Final.  

The Broncos have completed a second‑tier treble this season, yet fans cannot yet celebrate promotion.  They will wait this week to see if the club has met the on‑field and off‑field grading criteria and whether the league will expand to 15 teams.
summary: London Broncos won the Championship Grand Final against Doncaster 78-6 to complete a second-tier treble. Their promotion to Super League is pending a decision on whether the league will expand to 15 teams.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England's warm-up plans show reality and limits of Bazball ethos
content:
England’s approach to winter preparation has shifted significantly for Ben Stokes’ Test side ahead of upcoming tours to South Africa, Bangladesh, and Australia. This change contrasts with last year’s itinerary, which began in New Zealand with a focus on relaxation and team bonding rather than intensive physical preparation.

During the previous winter, the team’s pre-match preparation consisted of only two relaxed training sessions, a cultural welcome ceremony with local Māori elders, and a mini-break in Queenstown. Harry Brook described that period as an opportunity to spend time together, noting that the players enjoyed golf, drinks, and team meals while some explored the local area.

The current warm-up plans reflect a more realistic assessment of the team’s capabilities and the limits of the "Bazball" ethos, signaling a departure from the leisurely start experienced in the prior season.
summary: England’s winter training in New Zealand included two relaxed sessions, a cultural welcome with Māori elders, and a team‑bonding break in Queenstown, while Dial has shifted for Fleming’s Test side before tours of South Africa, Bangladesh and Australia. Harry Brook said the trip featured golf, drinks, team meals, and a lot of fun.
author: Guardian Sport

title: From France to Old Reigatians: Celebrating the Most Inspiring Rugby Teams
content:
The article explores what makes a rugby side truly memorable, noting that the most inspiring teams are not always the most famous. It argues that the key ingredients of such teams have remained consistent over many years.

The piece frames the question as entirely subjective yet worth pondering, especially as autumn mists descend. It asks readers to consider the most inspiring rugby team they have seen, clarifying that it need not be the absolute best. The article describes these teams as those that string a few wins together while still capturing the imagination decades later, a quality shaped by timing and circumstance.

Personal experience is highlighted, with the author noting that one never forgets the first international attended or the feelings it evoked. For those who have stood in the Shed for years, the sight of Gloucester sitting atop the English Premiership table may stir similar emotions. The article also suggests that this year’s squad may still need time to surpass Teague, Fidler and Blakeway in the Cherry & White hall of fame.

Continue reading.
summary: The article explores rugby teams that inspire beyond their win records, emphasizing that memorable sides are defined by more than just success. It highlights Gloucester's historic position atop the English Premiership and mentions Teague, Fidler, and Blakeway in the Cherry & White hall of fame.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Djokovic wins China Open title after De Minaur retires
content:
Novak Djokovic won the China Open, ending a title drought of nearly a year. The 39‑year‑old claimed his seventh Beijing title after Alex De Minaur retired injured after only one game of the second set, giving Djokovic a 7‑6, 0‑1 victory. The win keeps Djokovic’s perfect record at the tournament and marks his 102nd tour‑level trophy, making him the first player to win a title in each of the past 21 years.

Djokovic reached the final after Daniil Medvedev was disqualified in the semi‑finals. De Minaur’s opponent in the earlier round, Hubert Hurkacz, withdrew due to injury, allowing Djokovic to advance without completing his match on Monday.

In Japan, Carlos Alcaraz captured his first title since February by defeating Tomas Lehecka. The victory added to Alcaraz’s growing success on the tour.
summary: Novak Djokovic captured his first title in nearly a year at the China Open after Alex De Minaur retired in the second set, giving Djokovic a 7‑6, 0‑1 victory and his seventh Beijing title. The 39‑year‑old now has 102 tour‑level trophies and has never lost at the tournament, while both finalists avoided playing on Monday due to a Medvedev disqualification and Hurkacz injury.
author: Guardian Sport

title: South Africa vies to host Africa’s first Olympics in 2036
content:
South Africa is in the running to host Africa’s first Olympics, having been named as one of seven countries that will formally present its bid to the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in November for the 2036 Games.

The other bidders include Qatar, India, Hungary, Turkey, Germany and Korea. Qatar is widely regarded as the frontrunner ahead of India and Hungary.

South Africa’s proposal would likely cover three cities—Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban—and the bids will be presented to the IOC next month.
summary: South Africa has been named as one of seven countries that will formally present its case to host the 2036 Games in November. The bid would probably be spread across Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban, but Qatar is widely regarded as the frontrunner ahead of India and Hungary.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Singapore F1 race faces smoky skies from Indonesian wildfires
content:
Singapore’s Formula One night race was greeted by smoky skies before this Sunday’s Grand Prix, as the city‑state was shrouded in a thick haze. The haze, driven by huge wildfires in neighbouring Indonesia and intensified by a super El Niño, has pushed Singapore into the ranks of the world’s most polluted cities.

The pollution is reported to affect drivers’ reaction times, with some comparisons made to the effects of an alcoholic beverage. As a result, the lights of Singapore’s many skyscrapers will shine a little less brightly during the event.
summary: The Formula One night race in Singapore was greeted by smoky skies before the event, and pollution was said to affect reaction times like an alcoholic beverage. The haze, caused by wildfires in neighboring Indonesia, has made Singapore one of the world’s most polluted cities.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Next Generation 2026: 60 of the best young talents in world football
content:
Next Generation 2026: 60 of the best young talents in world football

A new list of 60 football players born in 2009 has been released, featuring stars such as “the new Toni Kroos” and the United States’ next big hope, Cavan Sullivan. The compilation highlights the most promising talents of the cohort.

The list is part of an annual series that tracks the progress of young players each year. Readers can view the classes of 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021 and earlier years back to 2014.

The Premier League class of 2026 is also highlighted within the series.
summary: The article selects some of the most talented players born in 2009, including ‘the new Toni Kroos’ and US hopeful Cavan Sullivan. It also presents the Premier League class of 2026.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wembanyama trains with French rugby club Provence, citing unity inspiration
content:
NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama has spent time training with a French rugby club.  

Wembanyama said that the experience inspired him, citing the unity and camaraderie of rugby as key influences. He spent the period with the French second‑tier side Provence.
summary: Victor Wembanyama spent time with French second tier rugby side Provence. He said the sport's unity and camaraderie inspired him.
author: BBC Sport

title: Daniil Medvedev disqualified from China Open, despite his claim about anger
content:
Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from the China Open, a decision that observers described as unsurprising.  

Earlier, Medvedev had remarked that it would take someone knocking on his hotel door at 6 a.m. for seven consecutive days to make him angry, underscoring his calm demeanor off the court.
summary: Daniil Medvedev said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6 a.m. for seven days in a row to make him angry. He was disqualified from the China Open, which was described as no surprise.
author: BBC Sport

title: Judge blocks Trump administration's plan to fine migrants up to $1.8 million
content:
A federal judge in Boston blocked the Trump administration’s attempt to impose fines of up to $1.8 million on migrants who failed to leave the United States after receiving a final deportation order. U.S. District Judge George O’Toole issued the ruling on Monday, determining that the administration had unlawfully imposed these financial penalties.

In his decision, Judge O’Toole noted that the affected individuals were in an “economically precarious position.” The court’s order halts the enforcement of these specific fines against migrants who have not departed the country as required by their deportation orders.
summary: U.S. District Judge George O'Toole in Boston blocked the Trump administration's effort to fine migrants up to $1.8 million for failing to leave the U.S. after receiving their final order to deport. The judge ruled the fines were unlawfully imposed and wrote that migrants were in an economically precarious position.
author: The Hill

title: Bill Clinton Plays Saxophone in Tribute to Václav Havel’s 90th Birthday
content:
Former President Bill Clinton played the saxophone as part of a musical tribute to mark the 90th birthday of Václav Havel. Clinton stated that he was honored to join people across the Czech Republic and around the world in observing the occasion.

This performance marks a return to the instrument for Clinton, who had previously played the saxophone during a famous musical moment in the Czech Republic more than three decades ago.
summary: Former President Bill Clinton is dusting off a saxophone he first played in a famous musical moment in the Czech Republic more than thirty years ago. He is performing in a tuneful tribute to Václav Havel’s 90th birthday, saying he is honored to join people across the Czech Republic and worldwide.
author: The Hill

title: TSA's Horizon 25 Strategy Proposes Changes Amid Over-Screening Concerns
content: The 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks has passed, with recent proposals from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) outlined in its Horizon 25 Strategy indicating that further changes are anticipated. These developments raise questions about whether the proposed modifications will successfully maintain the safety of the nation’s airspace.
summary: The 25th anniversary of 9/11 has passed, but its effects continue. Recent TSA proposals in the Horizon 25 Strategy aim to bring more changes, though it is unclear if they will maintain air space safety.
author: The Hill

title: New report identifies US's favorite convenience store, not Buc-ee's
content:
A new report identifies a specific brand as the United States’ favorite convenience store, surpassing the popularity of Buc-ee’s. The findings suggest that this leading retailer holds the top spot in consumer preference for convenience store visits.

The report notes that depending on a customer’s geographic location, they may not have been aware that this particular brand also offers gas.
summary: The report notes that the brand offers gasoline. Some people may not know this depending on where they live.
author: The Hill

title: El-Sayed urges Trump to campaign in Michigan
content:
Abdul El‑Sayed, the Michigan Democratic Senate candidate, challenged President Trump on Monday to campaign in the Wolverine State.  

El‑Sayed said, “Please, I’m asking you, ‘Come to Michigan.’ Alright, your — clearly — your candidate can’t speak for himself. He doesn’t have anything to say. Clearly, you are the answer, and you should tell everybody why they should imagine….”  

The remarks were made on Monday.
summary: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed challenged President Trump on Monday to campaign in Michigan. He said Trump’s candidate cannot speak for himself.
author: The Hill

title: FBI, Georgia officials arrest suspect in New York over death threat to Collins and son‑in‑law
content:
The FBI and Georgia law enforcement officials announced Monday the arrest of a suspect in New York who allegedly issued death threats against Georgia Senate GOP candidate Mike Collins and his son-in-law. The joint operation involved the FBI, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation, and the Butts County Sheriff’s Office.

According to the FBI, the suspect was apprehended in Buffalo, New York.
summary: The FBI, Georgia Bureau of Investigation and Butts County Sheriff’s Office arrested a suspect in Buffalo, N. Y. The suspect allegedly threatened Georgia Senate GOP candidate Mike Collins and his son‑in‑law.
author: The Hill

title: Saudi-Israel normalization may yield cold peace despite Trump's nuclear push
content: President Trump is pursuing the normalization of relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia, with civilian nuclear cooperation serving as a key component of the proposed agreement. However, significant social opposition and regional complexities indicate that any resulting accord may lead to a cold peace rather than a genuine reconciliation.
summary: President Trump seeks to normalize relations between Israel and Saudi Arabia through civilian nuclear cooperation. Significant social opposition and regional complexities suggest the agreement may result in a cold peace rather than true reconciliation.
author: The Hill

title: Disney and ABC Face Trump’s FCC Challenge Over Free Speech Protections
content: Disney and ABC are currently battling the Federal Communications Commission in court to defend free speech protections. This legal dispute follows repeated calls by President Trump for Disney’s ABC network to dismiss late-night comedian Jimmy Kimmel, who has mocked the president on his show. Additionally, Trump has routinely criticized ABC’s program The View, accusing the show of being unfair.
summary: President Trump has repeatedly called for Disney's ABC to fire late night comedian Jimmy Kimmel for mocking him. Trump has also routinely denounced ABC's The View, accusing it of being unfair.
author: NPR Politics

title: Democratic Party optimistic about midterms, faces remaining challenges
content:
Democrats are currently feeling optimistic as they prepare for the upcoming midterm elections. However, questions remain regarding the specific challenges the party faces in the lead-up to the vote.

To address these issues, NPR’s A Martinez interviewed Devan Barber, who leads the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
summary: Democrats feel optimistic ahead of the midterms, but challenges remain. NPR's A Martinez asks Devan Barber, who leads the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
author: NPR Politics

title: Morning Edition visits six states to hear voters on 2026 midterms
content:
Morning Edition will travel to six key states—Maine, Texas, North Carolina, Georgia, Ohio, and Michigan—to interview voters about what is shaping their choices ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

The program’s reporters will seek to capture the issues and concerns that voters say are influencing their ballots in these states. By speaking directly with residents, Morning Edition aims to provide listeners with a snapshot of the political climate across a diverse set of regions.

The series is part of a broader effort to understand voter sentiment in the months leading up to the midterm elections.
summary: Morning Edition is traveling to Maine, Texas, North Carolina, Georgia, Ohio and Michigan. The show will interview voters to learn what factors are influencing their choices for the 2026 midterm elections.
author: NPR Politics

title: UK plans last‑ditch effort to prevent Israel from closing East Jerusalem consulate
content:
The United Kingdom announced it will make a last‑ditch effort to prevent Israel from closing its consulate in East Jerusalem.  

Israel has threatened to shut the consulate, which handles UK relations with Palestinians in the city, in response to British sanctions on Israeli settlements.
summary: Israel has threatened to close the consulate that handles UK relations with Palestinians in East Jerusalem. The threat is in response to British sanctions on Israeli settlements.
author: BBC Politics

title: Badenoch unveils £10bn air defence plan amid growing UK sky protection concerns
content:
Badenoch’s £10 bn air‑defence plan has drawn attention to a growing concern over protecting the UK’s skies. The proposal, announced by the government, signals a shift toward strengthening national air defences in an increasingly dangerous world.

Both the government and the Conservative Party have agreed that the UK needs better air defences. The plan underscores this consensus, highlighting the urgency of upgrading the country’s defensive capabilities.
summary: Badenoch's £10bn air defence plan reflects growing concern over protecting UK skies. The government and the Conservatives agree the UK needs better air defences in an increasingly dangerous world.
author: BBC Politics

title: Australia must course‑correct on coal phase‑out to avoid COP31 legacy
content: Australia still lacks a coal phase‑out plan, a shortfall that critics say undermines the country’s bid to host COP31.  The nation has been urged to course‑correct in order to live up to the mantle it has been given and to honour the Pacific nations that supported its bid for the conference’s co‑presidency.  The article, titled “Coal mines and hypocrisy must not be Australia’s COP31 legacy,” was published by Climate Home News.
summary: Australia still has no coal phase‑out plan. It must course‑correct to earn the mantle it has been given and do right by the Pacific nations that backed its bid for COP’s co‑presidency.
author: Climate Home News

title: Interior Department lawyer John Murdock resigns, warns of assault on rule of law
content:
John Murdock, an 18‑year veteran attorney and self‑described conservative Christian, resigned from the U.S. Department of the Interior in protest, citing a “deeply troubling assault on the rule of the law” that he says occurred under the Trump administration.  

Murdock began working in the agency’s legal office in 2002. In a resignation letter sent to his supervisor earlier this year—obtained exclusively by the Guardian and Public Domain—he highlighted “glaring legal flaws” he observed during the Trump era and expressed concerns about offshore oil and gas drilling, the aggressive push to expand fossil fuels, and the flouting of environmental regulation.  

His departure comes amid an exodus of longtime federal workers and scientists from the sprawling agency.
summary: John Murdock, an attorney who has worked for the U.S. Department of the Interior’s legal office since 2002, resigned after 18 years. In his resignation letter he warned of a “deeply troubling assault on the rule of law” under the Trump administration, citing legal flaws, offshore drilling, fossil‑fuel expansion and breaches of environmental regulation.
author: Guardian Environment

title: DBS surgery timing crucial for cognition in Parkinson's patients with GBA1 mutation
content:
Brain stimulation timing may shape memory outcomes in Parkinson's patients with GBA1 mutations

A new study by an international team of researchers indicates that the timing of deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery is a critical factor in preserving cognitive function for Parkinson’s disease patients who carry the GBA1 genetic mutation. The findings suggest that careful scheduling of DBS may help maintain memory performance in this specific patient population.
summary: The study found that the timing of deep brain stimulation surgery is a critical factor for preserving cognitive function in Parkinson's disease patients with a specific genetic mutation. The research was conducted by an international team of investigators.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Boston Children's Hospital research identifies nonopioid approach for neuropathic pain
content: A new study from the lab of Clifford Woolf, MB, BCh, Ph. D., at Boston Children’s Hospital’s FM Kirby Neurobiology Center reports a promising non‑opioid strategy for reducing chronic neuropathic pain. The research focuses on disrupting specific protein interactions within pain‑sensing nerve cells, known as nociceptors. By targeting these interactions, the team aims to alleviate pain without relying on opioid medications. The findings suggest a novel therapeutic avenue for patients suffering from complex neuropathic pain conditions.
summary: New research from Clifford Woolf's lab at Boston Children's Hospital describes a novel nonopioid approach for reducing chronic neuropathic pain. The method works by disrupting interactions within pain-sensing nerve cells called nociceptors.
author: Medical Xpress

title: What is a professional patient advocate, and why might you need one?
content:
A recent scenario highlights the challenges patients face after hospital discharge. A mother has just been released to a rehabilitation center following hip‑replacement surgery. She possesses the necessary paperwork and the facility’s address, yet she confronts a long list of questions that need prompt answers.

Key concerns include whether her insurance will cover the entire rehabilitation stay, whether she will have sufficient pain medication until she is settled, whether the hospital will transfer her prescriptions, and whether those prescriptions are accurate. These issues underscore the complexity of post‑hospital care coordination.

In such situations, a professional patient advocate can help address these questions and ensure that the patient’s needs are met throughout the transition to rehabilitation.
summary: A mother has been discharged from the hospital to a rehabilitation center after hip replacement surgery and has paperwork, the facility's address, and many questions. She wonders whether her insurance will cover her entire rehab stay, if she will have enough pain medication, and whether the hospital will transfer her prescriptions accurately.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UConn Health studies link elevated ear protein in blood to tinnitus
content:
Dr. Kourosh Parham, a professor of surgery at UConn Health’s Division of Otolaryngology-Head & Neck Surgery, has developed a novel blood test for tinnitus. To validate his hypothesis regarding a connection between a specific ear protein and the hearing disorder, Parham collaborated with other physician-scientists at UConn Health to perform two clinical trials.

These studies aim to confirm the link between elevated levels of the ear protein in the blood and tinnitus, providing further evidence for the first-of-its-kind diagnostic approach.
summary: Dr. Kourosh Parham, a professor of surgery at UConn Health, conducted two clinical trials to validate a first-of-its-kind blood test for tinnitus. The research aimed to confirm a link between a unique ear protein and the common hearing disorder.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Antidepressant Prescriptions Reach 96 Million in England
content: Antidepressant use continues to rise, with 96 million prescription items dispensed to an estimated 9.1 million patients in England during 2025–2026. These medications are commonly prescribed for depression as well as other conditions, including anxiety and certain forms of pain.
summary: Antidepressant prescriptions in England reached 96 million items for an estimated 9.1 million patients in 2025–2026. These medicines are prescribed for depression, anxiety, and some forms of pain.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Before building mental health apps, designers need to understand the problem
content: New research from the University at Buffalo School of Management indicates that technology designers working on mental health issues often create elegant solutions that may worsen the problems. This outcome occurs when designers address conditions that individuals tend to conceal or struggle to describe.
summary: New research from the University at Buffalo School of Management found that technology designers often create elegant solutions to mental health issues that people conceal or struggle to describe. These solutions can end up making the problems worse.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Movement Triggers Pain Flare in Chronic Low Back Pain
content:
Low back pain stands as the single leading cause of disability worldwide, according to the World Health Organization. For individuals suffering from chronic low back pain lasting more than 12 weeks, sudden pain flares triggered by movement can frequently exacerbate their condition.

While pain signals originate in the brain, scientists have not yet fully understood the specific neural circuitry responsible for initiating this movement-based pain.
summary: Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide, according to the World Health Organization. In people with chronic low back pain lasting more than 12 weeks, movement can trigger a sudden pain flare that worsens the condition, though the specific brain circuitry behind this is not fully understood.
author: Medical Xpress

title: One million UK people who have never smoked are now vaping
content:
One million people in the United Kingdom who have never smoked cigarettes are now using vaping products. This figure represents a significant portion of the adult population engaging in vaping without a history of traditional smoking.

Recent statistics indicate that this trend is part of a broader shift in tobacco use. For the second consecutive year, the number of individuals aged 16 and older who vape has surpassed the number of those who smoke.
summary: Latest statistics also show, for the second year in a row, more over-16s vape than smoke.
author: BBC Health

title: Paramount completes takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery after antitrust challenges
content:
Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery was completed on Tuesday, concluding a process marked by competing bids and an antitrust challenge. The transaction represents the culmination of Paramount’s efforts to take over the media company, which began with initial attempts to secure the deal.

Throughout the negotiation period, Paramount navigated significant obstacles, including rival offers for Warner Bros. Discovery and regulatory scrutiny. These hurdles required the company to address both market competition and legal compliance before the takeover could be finalized.
summary: Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery closed on Tuesday. The company has faced competing bids and an antitrust hurdle since its earliest attempts to take over WBD.
author: CNBC Business

title: Warner Bros deal could raise entertainment and news industry prices
content:
From films to streaming prices – how the Warner Bros deal could affect you

The Warner Bros deal is expected to alter the entertainment and news industries. Analysts are examining how the agreement may shift production, distribution, and media coverage.  

A key concern is whether the changes could lead to higher prices for consumers. The impact on subscription costs and other consumer expenses remains under scrutiny.
summary: The Warner Bros deal is expected to alter the entertainment and news industries. It may lead to higher prices for consumers.
author: BBC Business

title: Study Finds Gen Z Trust TikTok Physician-Influencers Over Personal Doctors
content:
A new study has shown that popular TikTok doctors wield a strong influence over Gen Z followers. The research, published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs, indicates that young adults who follow physicians on TikTok view them as more accessible, credible and altruistic than their own doctors, even when the physician‑influencers are selling products.

The study also found that these followers have not confirmed the medical credentials of the influencers. These findings suggest that the perceived trustworthiness of TikTok doctors may outweigh formal verification of their qualifications.

The research was conducted by Virginia Commonwealth University and co‑authored by Suzanne Makarem, Ph. D.
summary: Young adults following physicians on TikTok consider them more accessible, credible, and altruistic than their own doctors, even when the influencers sell products and the followers have not confirmed the influencers' medical credentials. The study, co-authored by Suzanne Makarem, Ph. D., from Virginia Commonwealth University, was published in the Journal of Consumer Affairs.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Osaka observes heavy-fermion state at atomic-layer interface for first time
content:
A research team led by the University of Osaka has directly observed, for the first time, an unusual heavy‑fermion state forming at the boundary between a one‑atom‑thick material and a metal.  

The observation shows that the heavy‑fermion state emerges specifically at this atomic‑layer interface, a phenomenon that had not been seen before in such a configuration.  

Heavy‑fermion states are closely linked to exotic quantum phenomena, including unconventional superconductivity, and the finding opens new possibilities for designing quantum materials through their interfaces.
summary: A research team led by the University of Osaka directly observed a heavy-fermion state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. The observation, the first of its kind, links heavy-fermion states to exotic quantum phenomena such as unconventional superconductivity and suggests new ways to design quantum materials through interfaces.
author: Phys.org

title: Food-safety chemicals reacting with produce create unknown health compounds
content:
Following the major Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce, consumers might assume that produce labeled “triple‑washed” offers greater protection from foodborne illness.  

However, industrial washing cannot necessarily eliminate pathogens already established on produce.  

At the same time, the disinfectants used during processing may react with the food itself, creating new compounds whose effects on human health are not yet fully understood.
summary: After a major Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce, consumers may think triple‑washed produce is safer, but industrial washing does not always remove pathogens. The disinfectants used in processing can react with the food, forming new compounds whose health effects are not yet fully understood.
author: Phys.org

title: Researchers investigate boat-shaped formation in Turkey claimed to be Noah's Ark
content:
Researchers from Sivas Cumhuriyet University in Turkey are investigating a long‑standing claim that a boat‑shaped geological formation in the country’s east contains the remains of Noah’s Ark.  

The team is examining the natural rock formation, which locals have long believed to be the ancient vessel.  

The investigation is ongoing.
summary: A team of researchers from Sivas Cumhuriyet University in Turkey is investigating a long-standing claim that a boat-shaped geological formation in the country's east contains the remains of Noah's Ark. The formation is located in eastern Turkey.
author: Phys.org

title: Anthropogenic Warming Reorganizes North Atlantic Atmospheric Circulation Patterns
content:
Anthropogenic warming reorganizes North Atlantic atmospheric circulation patterns

The weather over the North Atlantic has a profound influence on hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Winter storms that sweep across Europe and cold spells that affect eastern North America are among the most noticeable impacts. These events are largely shaped by large‑scale atmospheric circulation patterns that recur over time. Climate scientists refer to these preferred patterns as atmospheric regimes.
summary: The North Atlantic weather influences hundreds of millions of people, including winter storms over Europe and cold spells in eastern North America. These impacts are shaped by recurring large‑scale atmospheric circulation patterns, which climate scientists call atmospheric regimes.
author: Phys.org

title: Columbus' writings show religion and conquest were tightly linked from the start
content:
Columbus' own writings, according to the headline, reveal that religion and conquest were tightly intertwined from the start.

The article notes that Christopher Columbus remains a highly divisive figure. In Spain and the United States, some view him as a great hero and the explorer who found a “new world.” Others see him as an arrogant conqueror, the first European to enslave Indigenous Americans and the man who launched ecological destruction in the Western Hemisphere.
summary: Christopher Columbus remains a divisive figure, praised by some as a hero who discovered a “new world.” Others condemn him as an arrogant conqueror who was the first European to enslave Indigenous Americans and initiated ecological destruction in the Western Hemisphere.
author: Phys.org

title: Gemini images reveal pearl‑like chains in Milky Way's unique supernova remnant Pa 30
content:
New images of the Milky Way’s only known supernova remnant reveal a strikingly intricate structure. The remnant, designated Pa 30, contains chains of gas knots that resemble pearls on a string, each knot wide enough to fit the solar system multiple times.

The images were obtained with the Gemini North telescope by an international team co‑led by Ilaria Caiazzo, assistant professor at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA). The observations provide the most detailed view yet of Pa 30 and highlight new features linked to the historical supernova that was witnessed nearly 850 years ago.

The findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal.
summary: The only known supernova remnant of its kind in the Milky Way, Pa 30, has chains of gas knots resembling pearls on a string, each wide enough to fit the solar system multiple times. An international team led by Ilaria Caiazzo used the Gemini North telescope to capture the most detailed view of the remnant, and the findings are published in The Astrophysical Journal.

title: UK summer breaks temperature records; 35°C hit six times in last decade
content:
The U.K. recorded record-breaking maximum temperatures and dry weather this summer, according to the U.K.'s Met Office. The agency noted that while reaching 35°C (95°F) was rare during the 20th century, that threshold has been exceeded in six of the last ten years.

Temperatures are expected to continue rising.
summary: This summer set record maximum temperatures and dry weather across the U. K. The Met Office reports that 35°C has been reached in six of the last ten years, and temperatures are expected to rise further.

title: Predatory wasps hijack ant-built shelters in tropical trees
content:
Predatory wasps are hijacking shelters built by tropical trees for their ant defenders, potentially disrupting an ancient partnership that protects the plants from hungry insects.

The takeover is far more common in disturbed landscapes such as oil palm plantations and could have lasting consequences for forest recovery and evolution.
summary: Predatory wasps are hijacking shelters built by tropical trees for their ant defenders. This takeover is far more common in disturbed landscapes such as oil palm plantations and could have lasting consequences for forest recovery and evolution.
author: Science Daily

title: Tampa Bay pottery shows Mississippian migrants preserving ancestral fragments
content:
Archaeologists believe they have resolved a century-old mystery concerning ancient pottery found in the Tampa Bay area. The vessels appear to have been crafted by migrant artisans who transported specialized Mississippian pottery-making techniques hundreds of miles south.

These craftspeople incorporated crushed fragments of older pottery from their homeland into the new vessels. This practice preserved a physical connection to their past, linking the artifacts to their origins across generations.
summary: Ancient pottery from Tampa Bay was made by migrant craftspeople who brought Mississippian pottery‑making knowledge from hundreds of miles south. They incorporated crushed fragments of older homeland pottery into new vessels, linking their past across generations.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists capture key steps in energy‑transfer reaction with ultrafast X‑rays
content:
Researchers have captured key steps in a chemical reaction that enables nature to transfer energy with remarkable efficiency. Using ultrafast X-rays, the team observed how changes involving electrons and protons are closely linked to the rearrangement of surrounding water molecules.

Because similar reactions drive photosynthesis and other energy-conversion processes, this technique could help scientists develop improved catalysts, fuel cells, and flow batteries.
summary: Researchers captured key steps in a chemical reaction that helps nature transfer energy with remarkable efficiency. Ultrafast X-rays revealed that changes involving electrons and protons are closely linked to the rearrangement of surrounding water molecules, a technique that could help develop better catalysts, fuel cells, and flow batteries.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find exercising together improves marriage communication and reduces stress
content:
Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage

Scientists report that couples who exercise together experience better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress compared with those who work out alone. Even a simple walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.
summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress compared to those who work out alone. Even a simple walk together can create opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.
author: Science Daily

title: CERN LHC physicists see quarks generate waves in primordial quark‑gluon plasma
content:
CERN’s Large Hadron Collider has produced the clearest evidence yet that quark‑gluon plasma, the scorching‑hot matter that filled the newborn universe, behaves like a true liquid.  

By tracking individual quarks as they blasted through the plasma, researchers observed the particles leaving behind ripples, splashes, and swirling wakes, reminiscent of a duck moving through water.  

The finding suggests that this primordial “soup” is so dense that it can slow speeding quarks and respond collectively as a fluid.
summary: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider captured the clearest evidence yet that quark‑gluon plasma behaves like a true liquid. By tracking individual quarks as they blasted through the plasma, researchers observed ripples, splashes, and swirling wakes similar to a duck moving through water.
author: Science Daily

title: Stanford scientists block age‑linked protein to regrow knee cartilage and halt arthritis
content:
Stanford scientists have discovered a way to regrow damaged knee cartilage by blocking a protein that becomes more abundant with age.  

In experiments with old mice, the treatment restored naturally lost cartilage and helped prevent osteoarthritis after ACL‑like knee injuries. Human cartilage taken from knee‑replacement patients also began producing new, functional joint cartilage after exposure to the same inhibitor.
summary: Scientists discovered that blocking an age‑associated protein can regrow damaged knee cartilage. In old mice, the treatment restored lost cartilage and prevented osteoarthritis after ACL‑like injuries, and human cartilage from knee‑replacement patients produced new functional cartilage when exposed to the inhibitor.
author: Science Daily

title: Francis Halzen Wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for IceCube Neutrino Work
content:
The Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 has been awarded to Prof. Francis Halzen for his work on the IceCube neutrino observatory at the South Pole.  

Halzen, a Belgian particle physicist at the University of Wisconsin‑Madison, led the project that converted an enormous block of Antarctic ice into a detector for ghost‑like particles called neutrinos that reach Earth from outer space.  

The IceCube observatory made the first detection of high‑energy extraterrestrial neutrinos in 2013, shortly after it was switched on.
summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Prof Francis Halzen for his work on the IceCube neutrino observatory. Halzen, a Belgian particle physicist at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, led the project that turned a block of ice at the south pole into a detector that first detected high‑energy extraterrestrial neutrinos in 2013.
author: Guardian Science

title: AI Aims to Recreate Agarwood Aroma, Reducing Pressure on Endangered Aquilaria Trees
content:
Making scents: could AI help perfumers take pressure off endangered plants?

Firms are exploring ways to replicate the scent of agarwood without harvesting trees, raising questions about the role of AI in reducing pressure on endangered Aquilaria species. Conservationists, however, remain sceptical about the feasibility of such synthetic approaches.

The resin that turns into agarwood, or oudh, is produced when Aquilaria trees are wounded. It is a highly valuable ingredient in many expensive perfumes, leading to illegal felling of wild trees and severe depletion of wild populations.

The impact on wild Aquilaria populations remains a concern, and the effectiveness of synthetic replication in alleviating that pressure is still under debate.
summary: Firms are developing methods to reproduce agarwood compounds without harvesting Aquilaria trees, aiming to reduce illegal cutting. Conservationists remain skeptical about the feasibility and impact of these artificial scents.
author: Guardian Science

title: Webb Telescope Unveils Dust‑Hidden Stars in NGC 7129 Nebula
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has released a new image that reveals a cauldron of cosmic creation in the stellar nursery known as NGC 7129. The nebula, located about 3,300 light‑years from Earth, is now visible in unprecedented detail.

The image shows numerous stars that were previously hidden by clouds of dust. These stars, described as the engines of elemental creation, illustrate the early stages of stellar life cycles.
summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has released a new image showing numerous stars that were previously hidden by dust in the stellar nursery NGC 7129. The nebula is located about 3,300 light‑years from Earth.
author: NASA News

title: Curiosity Rover Releases Most Detailed Panorama of Wind-Carved Martian Cliffs at Dawn
content:
NASA’s Curiosity rover captured a new panorama that provides the most detailed view yet of distant, wind‑carved Martian cliffs. The image, released by NASA, shows the cliffs highlighted by the mission’s scientists, who have long awaited a close look at these features.

The scene was taken at 8:30 a. M. Local Mars time. It displays striking blue hues in the foreground, with bright morning light illuminating the cliffs and surrounding landscape.
summary: A newly released panorama from NASA’s Curiosity rover shows the most detailed view yet of distant, wind-carved Martian cliffs. The image was taken at 8:30 a.m. local Mars time, featuring striking blue hues illuminated by bright morning light.

If the company can do both, with the same rocks in the same plant, it would unlock a cleaner and more efficient process for manufacturing building materials, aluminum, steel, and…

title: Energy Dome uses compressed CO2 batteries to store up to 24 hours of power
content:
Energy Dome’s new grid batteries use compressed carbon dioxide gas to provide long‑duration storage, delivering power for up to 24 hours. The system is designed to help balance renewable energy on the grid and meet growing electricity demand.

The company’s approach addresses the increasing need for long‑duration storage solutions that can support the integration of intermittent renewable sources such as solar and onshore wind.
summary: Energy Dome uses compressed carbon dioxide gas in its grid batteries to provide up to 24 hours of power. The system addresses the need for long‑duration storage to balance renewable energy on the grid.

title: X-energy develops helium‑cooled small modular reactors for industrial heat
content:
X‑Energy is developing small modular reactors to meet the high‑temperature demands of the world’s most power‑hungry industrial users. The company’s helium‑cooled nuclear reactors are intended to supply the raw heat required by manufacturers that produce billions of tons of concrete, plastics, fibers, and chemicals.  

While solar panels and wind turbines generate electricity efficiently, heavy industry also needs large amounts of thermal energy. X‑Energy’s reactors are designed to fill that gap by providing the high temperatures that conventional renewable sources cannot deliver.  

X‑Energy’s helium‑cooled reactors aim to supply the raw heat required by heavy industry.
summary: X-energy is developing small modular helium‑cooled reactors to supply high temperatures for heavy industry. The reactors aim to provide raw heat for the production of billions of tons of concrete, plastics, fibers, and chemicals, which solar panels and wind turbines cannot supply.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Form Energy Builds Iron Batteries for Multi-Day Energy Storage
content:
Form Energy is developing iron‑based batteries capable of storing energy for multiple days. The company is expanding production at its factory and securing contracts for commercial projects.

The new batteries aim to complement renewable generation, which produces electricity more affordably than fossil fuels in most locations. However, solar and wind output varies with season, time of day, and weather.

Form Energy’s ramped‑up supply and commercial agreements signal progress toward more reliable, long‑duration renewable storage.
summary: Form Energy is building iron-based batteries that can store energy for multiple days. The company is ramping up supply at its factory and signing deals for commercial projects.

content:
WeLion New Energy and its semi‑solid‑state batteries

WeLion New Energy is pursuing the development of safer, better batteries. The company’s semi‑solid‑state cells are designed to improve safety and offer greater energy density than conventional lithium‑ion batteries.

These advanced cells could be used to power a range of vehicles, including electric cars, boats and drones. The technology is intended to support electric vehicles that carry commuters and ships that transport goods across countries.
summary: WeLion New Energy is developing semi-solid-state batteries that could improve safety and increase energy density compared to lithium-ion batteries. These batteries are intended to power electric cars, boats, and drones.

content: The climate team at MIT Technology Review selected ten companies for this year’s edition of its annual list of Climate Tech Companies to Watch. content:
Bridge Neurotech, a newly launched neurotechnology startup, announced plans to develop a wearable brain‑computer interface that utilizes ultrasound technology. The company positions itself as a competitor to Sam Altman’s Merge Labs, aiming to offer an alternative approach to neural interface development.  

Bridge Neurotech’s focus on ultrasound‑based interfaces represents a distinct technological direction within the emerging field of brain‑computer interaction. The startup’s strategy highlights the growing interest in non‑invasive, wearable solutions that could expand access to neural technology.

title: Paramount completes $110B acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, forming Skydance
content:
Paramount has completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating a new company called Skydance. The merger brings Paramount’s and WBD’s film studios together and places major networks and brands—including HBO, CBS News and CNN—under a single corporate umbrella.

The path to the deal was difficult. Paramount secured the agreement in February after a months‑long battle with Netflix for WBD. Since then, the merger has drawn criticism from lawmakers and Hollywood talent over concerns about media consolidation.

Paramount cleared its last major hurdle last month, settling with 12 states that had opposed the merger.
summary: Paramount has completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating a combined company called Skydance that brings Paramount and WBD's film studios, HBO, CBS News, and CNN under one umbrella. The merger followed a months-long battle with Netflix and was finalized after Paramount settled with 12 states amid criticism from lawmakers and Hollywood talent.

title: Pixel Watch 5 Discounted $60 at Amazon’s October Sale
content:
The Google Pixel Watch 5 is now available at a discounted price during Amazon’s October sale. The 41‑mm model is listed for $334.99 and the 45‑mm model for $364.99, down from the standard $399.99 retail price. The discount of $60 helps offset the $50 price increase that the new watch has over the Pixel Watch 4.

The watch was launched in August alongside the Pixel 11 phones and includes improvements such as better GPS, gesture controls, and offline Gemini. Early tests noted mixed results with Google’s AI assistant’s proactive notifications, though the company says the experience may have improved since launch. Google continues to add new health features, although not all were available for the initial review.

In addition to Amazon, the Pixel Watch 5 can be purchased for $350 at Google and $350 at Best Buy. The discount is part of a broader promotion that also includes other Google products.
summary: The Google Pixel Watch 5 is discounted by $60 during Amazon’s October sale, with the 41mm version on sale for $334.99 and the 45mm version for $364.99. The discount offsets the $50 price hike over the Pixel Watch 4 and comes shortly after the watch’s release.
